finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.docusign.com/mcp answers 403 with the 19-byte plain-text body "RBAC: access denied" and no www-authenticate header: the refusal names no realm, no metadata URL and no way in. The RFC 9728 default path for the resource answers the same 403 with the same body, so the access gate sits in front of the discovery document as well as the server, and a client following the current MCP authorization specification finds nothing to read. The one thing the host serves keyless is its tool catalog: GET /tools answers 200 with a JSON-RPC result of 22 tools (envelopes, templates, recipients, users, Maestro workflow instances), each with a description, an input schema and annotations. A keyless GET on the account server's userinfo endpoint answers 400 with an internal_server_error body, not the 401 a missing token usually earns. Same 403 and same public catalog as the 2026-09-13 measurement in the entry's notes; the gated discovery path and the userinfo status are recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what the server does with a credential.
